newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia shares firm, pushed up by foreign demand.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia shares firm, pushed up by foreign demand.

text.p: Slovenia's blue-chip SBI index firmed 0.38 percent on Tuesday as foreign investors flirted with the market but traders foresaw little change over the next two weeks due to the summer holidays.

"Stronger foreign demand brought fresh optimism and pulled prices up but that will not be enough for continuous growth," one trader said. "Demand is not likely to remain strong this week due to the holidays."
The SBI index firmed 5.83 points, or 0.38 percent, to 1,540.67.
Drug maker Lek was most actively traded, up 0.99 percent to 35,600 tolars on volume of 8,537 shares for total turnover of 303 million tolars.
Overall eight shares rose, one was unchanged, five fell and 14 were untraded. Turnover jumped to 362 million tolars from 201.8 million.
Financial consultancy Dadas was the top gainer, up 10 percent to 6,490 tolars on volume of 30 shares but traders said its growth could be short-lived due to the share's poor liquidity.
Preferred shares in trader Kovinotehna were the leading decliner, down 10 percent to 450 tolars on volume of just 855 shares.
Analysts pinpointed liquid shares like Lek and petrol trader Petrol as the safest investment at the moment, joined by drug maker Krka, which is listed on the over-the-counter (OTC) market.
